chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yunus, from Sabbah ibn Sabih, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'If a man intends to perform the Friday prayer and recites 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' [in the first rak'ah],' he said, 'He completes it as two rak'ahs, then he starts anew [for the remaining two rak'ahs].'

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Surah Al-Ikhlas, the 112th chapter of the Quran)
key_terms.يُتِمُّهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ: He completes it as two rak'ahs

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one only recites Surah Al-Ikhlas during Friday prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a worshipper who recites only Surah Al-Ikhlas during the Friday prayer, establishing that the prayer is valid but incomplete. The Imam instructs that the individual must complete the prayer as a two-rak'ah unit and then perform two additional rak'ahs to fulfill the four-rak'ah requirement of Dhuhr, highlighting the flexibility in recitation while maintaining structural integrity. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that omitting a full Surah does not invalidate the prayer but affects its completeness, requiring compensation through additional units.
